title: SANCTIFICATION
mv: And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
mvp: “And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” 1Thessalonians 5:23
assignment: List five (5) practical ways a believer can daily live a sanctified life (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Sanctification is a spiritual surgery performed by God in the life of a saved soul (Ezekiel 36:26). It is the second work of grace after salvation. Sanctification simply means to make holy, pure and separated unto God (Jeremiah 1:4-5). It is a progressive work of God in man that makes us free from sin and be like Christ (1 Thessalonians 5:23; Romans 8:13). It is vital to understand the process and benefits of sanctification.

To be sanctified, you need to see yourself as you are; filthy and in need of help, after which you cry to God for deliverance (Isaiah 6:5). Present yourself to the Sanctifier - God (1Thessalonians 5:23), through the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:2; 2 Thessalonians 2:13), the word of God (John. 17:17), the blood of Jesus (Hebrews 9:13-14; 1 John. 1:7, 9), and daily surrender (Colossians 3:8-10; Romans 6:13). This process can be a painful experience but the result is that you are broken and transformed into a new nature (Galatians 2:20; 2Timothy 2:3-4). The awareness that you do not own yourself anymore helps you prioritise God in everything you do, and whatever does not glorify Him is a no-go area for you (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).

Sanctification represents a believer’s victory over the flesh (Romans 7:24-25), the world (1John 5:4), and the devil (James 4:7). A sanctified believer will enjoy the ability to easily resist temptation because there is a renewed hatred for sin and lust. Sanctification fosters intimacy with God, increases spiritual strength and stability (Psalm 15:1-5). It also aids ‘clean record’ for believers, that is, the enemy will not have a foothold over such (John 14:30). It helps believers to be humble and submissive to God and to constituted authorities. The Adamic nature in man is subdued (Romans 8:1-5). It gives the believer control over self (Galatians 2:20; Romans 6:13). It promotes right standing before God and pure intentions of actions and words (Acts 24:16).
Sanctification is an integral part of Christian growth; every child of God must earnestly desire it.
